Senses.Note: One block counted as one thing: the birth dialogue, two warning lists, a sickness ban, a contrast address, an installation address, a night-talk ruling, a staged-definition refutation, an occasional verse, and a farewell confession all spend the same four graphs on the same hermit's night. The root master of the birth dialogue (Yunju Daojian, second abbot of the mountain) is not roster-listed; his family rides as an anchor claiming the 1004 lamp's bytes only, and the eight own-record families carry the entry without it. The essay use that lodges the pratyekabuddha alone on the solitary peak, watching conditions scatter, self-awakening to the unborn, spends the graphs in a different, literal sense and stays out of the entry.

Senses.Explanation: The four graphs name the hermit's night - lodging alone on a solitary peak - and the corpus prices that night from birth: the earliest witness refuses it, the seven-bay monks' hall standing empty in the birth dialogue of the Jingde lamp; two warning lists - the one in the record of Linji, and the Deshan address preserved inside the letter of Dahui - fold it among austerities that still make karma; the summer-close instruction of Langye Huijue names it the second of five sicknesses; and the later masters - Huitang Zuxin, Yuanwu Keqin, Xiatang Huiyuan, Zhongfeng Mingben, Tianru Weize and Zongbao Daodu - spend it as the priced pole of the withdrawal-and-engagement pair. Born refused. The block enters the record as a question - (問孤峯獨宿時如何) - and the answer turns it back on the asker: the seven-bay monks' hall left unslept-in, (阿誰教汝孤峯獨宿) - who told you to? Linji's own record files the block into his warning list - dawn-fast, long sitting through the night, six periods of walking the way - all of it (皆是造業底人), people making karma; Deshan's address, preserved verbatim inside Dahui's letter, runs the same list with six periods of recitation and doubting birth-and-death. Langya Huijue opens his record's summer-close instruction by naming five sicknesses, and the block is the second: (二不得孤峯獨宿), with the rule that one blocked place leaves self-rescue impossible. Priced as one pole. The masters who keep the block trade it against its opposite. Huitang Zuxin: if you go along sounding-and-echoing, I will denounce the quarters; if you put on the taverns and the brothels, I will lodge alone on the solitary peak - then his Huanglong-eye question. Yuanwu Keqin's installation address prices both exclusives - always alone, eyes on the clouds: too high; always at the crossroads, dust-faced: too humiliating - and resolves them: one of awakened understanding can lodge alone on the solitary peak without obstruction from dust-faced work, and work dust-faced without obstruction from the solitary peak. Xiatang Huiyuan's verse for the new abbot taking Tianzhu temple runs the pair inside one rhyme - hand-in-hand walking, lodging alone on the solitary peak - and closes: that upper-person can hardly follow the lofty tracks. Re-read, not renounced. Zhongfeng Mingben's night talk answers why the awakened ancients differed - some lodging alone, some dropping hands into the market, some never meeting a single person: the sameness is what they awakened to, the difference is each one's karmic conditioning - not love of quiet that lodges alone, not fondness for crowds that enters the market. Tianru Weize stages a guest who defines pure reclusion by the block - lodge alone, deep in a thatched hut, one oar on the misty waves, ten-thousand pines and a house of cloud - and answers: you are stuck on the trace; the absolute reading finds pure reclusion even mingling with the filth and standing before the multitudes. Zongbao Daodu's farewell address names it as the road not taken: since youth his intention was to lodge alone on the solitary peak, but things did not follow his wish - his Boshan master (博山先師) had seen through him years before. What the block does: it names the withdrawal end of the pair at its most concrete - one person, one peak, one night - so that each speaker can price it. The record's prices run from refusal (the empty hall) through karma-listing and sickness-banning to role-exchange, both-ways freedom, conditioning, un-sticking, and confession; the peak itself never changes, only the price.

Gaofeng Yuanmiao owns the retained deployment: because a chan practicer had an awakening he ascends the hall - twenty years and more he has spread a sky-covering net to snare phoenixes and dragons and never met even a shrimp or crab; now a gnats'-midge worm has blundered in, unfit for the eye, yet thirty years hence on the solitary peak's very summit it will raise its voice and shout, and what does it shout: the great earth's mountains and rivers, one expanse of snow.

Senses.Explanation: The solitary summit marks an exposed or withdrawn extreme that records contrast with responsive activity at the crossroads or in the noisy market. Shenfeng Xian supplies the peak-versus-market contrast deployment through direct contrast between reviling buddhas on the peak and following sound in the market. Jie'an Jin supplies the reversible peak-and-crossroads practice deployment through direct reversible pairing of the summit and the crossroads. Jieshi Zhipeng supplies the seasonal heightened-exposure image deployment through direct seasonal hall-address use of the summit's heightened exposure. Baichi Xingyuan supplies the peak-rest versus long-street engagement deployment through direct contrast between resting on the summit and dragging through mud in the long street.

Senses.Explanation: On the summit of a solitary peak: an image for isolated transcendence, often set against activity in the crossroads. Linji poses the peak and crossroads as two alternatives; later masters use the pair to test freedom in seclusion and action. Yinyuan, Baiyu, Hanxiu, and Tianan give distinct current applications. Retained public meaning is supported by independent present uses in recorded discourse.

Complete Five Lamps (Vols. 34–120) (五燈全書(第34卷-第120卷)): Miaozhan Wenzhao's explicitly headed section, Miaozhan Wenzhao asks whose radiance is distinctly solitary and warns that answering with suchness or ultimate reality cuts a wound in sound flesh.

Senses.Explanation: Brightness or clarity described as standing by itself and remaining unmistakably distinct. Its common expansions make the constraint explicit: 'brightness standing alone, distinct and distinct' (孤明歷歷) and 'brightness standing alone and shining by itself' (孤明獨照). Linji Yixuan identifies 'the person right now before your eyes, listening... distinct and distinct' (即今目前孤明歷歷地聽者此人). Dahui Zonggao likewise describes people sitting and standing plainly in that distinct clarity while speaker and listener meet. The records refuse to make the description a terminus: Xueyan Zuqin says that profound clarity and distinct brightness standing alone 'is not yet news of arriving home' (未是到家消息). Miaozhan Wenzhao asks, 'Whose radiance is this distinct brightness standing alone?' (歷歷孤明，是誰光彩), then warns that calling it 'true suchness and the actual limit' (真如實際) resembles cutting a sore into sound flesh. The term therefore describes a salient, self-standing clarity in these passages without naming a completed attainment or a procedure.

Senses.Explanation: The phrase names a brightness that stands alone and is plainly distinct. Feiyin pairs seeing it with hearing sounds without confusion; Dafang places it beside openness and continuity; Lanshi sets it in a verse line where the many workings are empty. Xueyan supplies the limit: he says that such brightness is not yet news of arrival.

Occurrences.Kwic: 云：直是裩無襠、袴無口，頭上青灰三五斗，也未夢見在。饒你東西不辯、南北不分，眼似眉毛、口如鼻孔，養得如嬰兒純純地，也未夢見在。還會麼？風定花猶落，鳥啼山更幽。萬法齊觀歸復自然萬法齊觀歸復自然拈云：了了見無一物，天地一指，萬物一馬，懷六合於胸中而靈鑑有餘，鑑萬象於方寸而其神常虗，不動纖毫，一時成現，孤明獨照，歷劫坦然，返本還源，歸根復命，到這裏方合自然天真之道。若能如是，是真出家。泯其所以不可方比泯其所以不可方比拈云：若更開口，堪作什麼？所以道：萬象既泯，全體露現。正當恁麼時，說似一物即不中，喚作一物即不可，類不齊，不稱斷，混不得，亘古今。如人飲水，冷暖自知，不可說示於人。諸人者要會麼？鷺鶿立雪非同色，明月芦花不似它。

Senses.Explanation: “Solitary brightness shining alone” describes a light or awareness presented as isolated in its shining. The records use the phrase in warnings and appraisals and contrast it with encounter, response, or the surrounding field where those contrasts are explicitly stated.

Senses.PreferredTarget: solitary and poor
Senses.Explanation: A paired description of being without support and without means. In the public case, Qingshui (清稅) tells Caoshan Benji, “Qingshui is solitary and poor; I beg Caoshan Benji for relief” (清稅孤貧。乞師賑濟。). Caoshan Benji calls him forward and tells him that after three cups of the Bai-family wine he still says his lips are dry. Later verses retain the ordinary force of the words: Yinyuan Longqi writes of “one solitary, poor monk,” Konggu Daocheng of a poor traveler who does not borrow prestige, and Yuanjie Jingying of begging to be pitied for this poverty. The cited texts do not define a separate condition called “poverty in spirit.”
Senses.Note: The Qingshui-Caoshan exchange is one inherited case despite its many recensions. Independent poems by named masters support the same paired description without turning it into another sense.

Occurrences.Kwic: 歸眾，師乃云：「德厚心慈，量寬行廣，開人天之眼目，作衲子之紀綱，在今時中惟我雪峰和尚法兄一人而已。山僧昔出其門，自念深恩未報，刻銘五內，朝夕弗忘，不謂去秋法幢遽隕，慧日掩光，偶接訃音，籲天躄地。「諸仁者！汝且道：雪峰和尚安身在什麼處？若道伊不生不滅、無去無來，那箇不知？若道伊此方緣盡，他方顯化，阿誰不會？若道只此不知不會便是雪峰和尚安身處，轉覺沒交涉。還委悉麼？」下座，煩兩序大眾同到靈前設奠燒香，普禮三拜。師五旬，聖念請上堂。「夢眼纔開，挨過浮生半百；腳跟有據，踏翻剎海三千。活潑潑，圓陀陀，八風吹而不動；峭巍巍，孤迥迥，劫火燒以長存。入佛、入魔，可凡、可聖，且道：是何人分上事？」以拄杖作撫琴勢，云：「高山流水許誰知？知音獨憶鍾子期。」上堂。僧問：「天上碧桃和露種，日邊紅杏倚雲栽，還許攀折也無？」師云：「汝試攀折看。」進云：「西望瑤池降王母，東來紫氣滿函關。」師云：「閑言長語，這裏用不著。」進云：「今日與師親祝壽，橫吹鐵笛，賀太平去也。」師云：「笑汝者多。」問：「高陞寶座，四眾臨筵，佛法當陽，如何施設？」師云：「昨日雨，今日晴。」進云：「當機覿面提，覿面當機疾，不犯好手，更請一接。」師默然。僧喝，師云：「鼓粥飯氣。」進云：「請接則且置，喻如師遠來慶誕，未審和尚還受慶也無？」

Occurrences.Kwic: 逐鬧趨時，始可承先裕後？明芳愚懦無知，自少隨波逐浪。因叨知己激勵，指參心地法門。趨向雖堅，習氣深重。不是病魔作難，便為熟境牽纏。猶幸緊著草鞋，直入五雲深處。四威儀內，無非孤峻鉗鎚；二六時中，常示人天師範。一夜大夢忽醒，摸著娘生鼻孔。始知面目儼然，多費常住鹽醬。既然如是，則一超直入，萬行莊嚴。淨穢悉圓覺伽藍，寂喧皆彌勒樓閣。又要閉關作甚麼？良久，起身曰：敢煩大眾同到關前，聽明芳再為露布。便入。龍聖龍門濟禪師龍聖龍門濟禪師三山陳氏子。示眾。泉鳴㵎底，風響枝頭，西來祖意，全放全收。你等諸人更覓甚麼碗？拈杖旋風打散。示眾。孤迥迥，無變易，石人夜半競吹笛，曉來門啟興翛然，山自青兮水自碧。更思借火添燈，只向他道不必。小參。不是心，不是佛，不是物，陝府鐵牛眼突出，嘉州大象忽擡頭，󳬧子飛過新羅國。更有踏斷草鞵跟，掀翻坐具地，到者裏，山僧直須驗過了打。何故？嚥津絕粒非為妙，換骨丹成始是仙。示眾。狗子佛性有，衣破露出肘；狗子佛性無，滄海竭底枯。若能于此知端的，看破趙州好大哥。良久，曰：大眾還知端的麼？搖頭擺尾非他物，莫向旁人問有無。問：盡大地是某甲本來面目，是否？師指路邊松，曰：喚者個作甚麼？僧擬對，師遽行。問：如何是古佛心？師曰：汝身得與麼矮小？僧

AlternateTargets: These thoughts are unreal, and so the cycle continues

Occurrences.Kwic: 故經云：『一切眾生皆由不知性淨明體，用諸妄想，此想不真，故有輪轉。』若不勇猛做一番工夫，要解脫修行，誠未有日子在。

ActorAttribution.GrammarEvidence: The original T19n0945 passage at0106c29 explicitly places this explanation after Buddha speaks to Ananda. The retained scripture citation reproduces that named reply, while the following application belongs to the current teacher.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J25/J25nB171.xml). Recorded Sayings of Monk Tianyin. Tianyin Yuanxiu addresses laywomen living in wealth and urges inquiry into the original face before their parents' birth while managing households, receiving guests, dressing and eating. A scripture says beings fail to know their pure luminous nature and use imagined thoughts: because these thoughts are untrue, continued wandering follows. He therefore urges immediate practice, citing the determined widow who became Wuzhuo, rather than waiting for family business to be finished. The quoted Buddha's explanation supplies a reason for urgency amid domestic responsibilities; it does not establish that wealth itself prevents realization or that merely abandoning the household would complete the work.

Occurrences.Kwic: 晚參。「結制已三日也，棒打石人頭，嚗嚗論實事。如何是實事？一切眾生生死相續，皆由不知常住真心、性淨明體，用諸妄想。此想不真，故有輪轉。」以拄杖畫一畫，云：「截斷你腳跟，擉瞎你眼睛，常住真心，性淨明體在甚麼處？」良久，喝一喝，云：「莫妄想。」
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J26/J26nB187.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Tian’an Sheng. Three days into retreat, Tian'an Sheng asks what the real matter is and revoices the scripture's account: beings continue through birth and death because they do not know the enduring true mind and use unreal imaginings. Drawing with his staff, he says he cuts off their footing and blinds their eyes, then asks where this enduring true mind and pure luminous substance are. After a pause he shouts and tells them not to imagine. His present challenge prevents the scriptural names becoming another object to grasp; the violent wording accompanies a staff gesture and does not report actual mutilation of a listener.

Occurrences.Kwic: 上堂。「新豐一句，當陽道破，不涉唇吻，已成露布。細雨濛濛，黃花滿路，打失衲僧鼻孔，忘卻邯鄲故步。古鏡臺前，幾多錯誤。大眾！一切眾生皆繇不知常住真心、性淨明體，用諸妄想，此想不真，故有輪轉。且道既不用諸妄想，畢竟用箇甚麼？」左右顧大眾云：「骼。」
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J27/J27nB189.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Sanyi Yu. Sanyi Mingyu begins with Xinfeng's sentence disclosed before speech and a rainy scene of yellow flowers, then warns of errors before the ancient mirror. He revoices the scriptural explanation of unreal imagining and continued wandering, but immediately asks: if one does not use these imaginings, what does one use? He looks left and right at the assembly and ends with a terse sound represented by a single character. The question makes the apparently simple prohibition of thought into a present demand. The closing sound is not explained in the source and should not be expanded into a secure positive name for a special faculty beyond thought.

Occurrences.Kwic: 上堂。「汝等當知，一切眾生從無始來生死相續，皆由不知常住真心，性淨明體，用諸妄想。此想不真，故有輪轉。且道念底是甚麼？秖恨釋迦老子不見吾狂耳。」
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J36/J36nB369.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Zhe’an Fan. Zhe'an Jingfan revoices the scripture's account of enduring mind obscured by unreal imaginings and then asks what it is that thinks. He says he regrets Shakyamuni cannot witness his wildness, takes up his staff and calls this his true acquaintance, relieving loneliness with an affinity across past and present. How can he convey the message to travelers in the three realms? He strikes his staff and answers with the east's two cyclical signs. The scriptural line leads into his own question and object demonstration; the staff is not automatically identified as the metaphysical substance named in the quotation.

Occurrences.Kwic: 不見《首楞嚴經》云：『一切眾生從無始來生死相續，皆由不知常住真心、性淨明體，用諸妄想。此想不真，故有輪轉。』釋迦老子秪為慈悲之故，故有落草之談。

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J40/J40nB494.xml). Recorded Sayings of Monk Yushan. At the third seven-day memorial for Tianjing Che, Yushan Shangsi explicitly quotes the Surangama Scripture's explanation that unreal imaginings produce continued wandering. He calls this Shakyamuni's compassionate accommodation, then says a Chan monk must sweep even enduring true mind and pure luminous substance onto the rubbish heap before overturning the opposed mountains and seas of final release and birth-and-death. He praises Tianjing's long practice and death, ending with a vow-oriented verse about future meeting with Maitreya and renewing the ancestral transmission. This is a memorial evaluation and exhortation, not independent proof of the deceased's realization or a simple denial that the scripture has any teaching value.

Entries.SourceTerm: 此方真教體，清淨在音聞

Senses.PreferredTarget: In this realm, the true medium of the teaching is sound and hearing in their purity
AlternateTargets: For this land, the true teaching medium lies in pure sound and hearing
SearchAliases: true teaching medium sound and hearing
Senses.Note: The line, cited from scripture in the recorded talks, places this realm's true teaching medium in sound and hearing. Several masters make listeners hear a present strike or bell, while Azi warns against treating passing sound itself as the whole point.

Occurrences.Kwic: 其傑之尤也。信根既深，把捉既定，就語言文字上東嚼西咬，驀忽洗面摸著鼻，盡將自得不傳之妙方便轉作為人，此其傑之次也。若夫生無傑才，莽莽蕩蕩，輕蔑因果，甘處凡庸，譬猶撮糞積成塿阜，徒增穢臭，要望崚嶒傑出驢年去。古有傑峰愚，西安余氏子也，參止巖悟道，偈云：「夜半忽然忘月指虛空，迸出日輪紅。」後開法，福慧龍象，駢臻禪人。今自易號為傑峰，意亦羨此歟？幸刪舊染而毋徒飾乎虛名。耳融說耳融說新蛙吠月，嫩竹敲風，步出松門之外靜坐片時，悠然若有所得也。因思此方真教體，清淨在音聞，從聞證入，獲大圓通，剎剎塵塵渾融無礙，古聖人垂慈闡化，顯意立言，利益功綦深哉。良由眾生顛倒，迷己逐物，雖本聞真聲日常現前，非是耳邊蹉過，便覺胸中凝滯，欲其旋聞返本，了了融通，詎可及耶？禾能仁聞禪者字耳？融偶寄一紙需予說，予嬾甚麾筆硯，半春矣，乃舉向之所得者以相告，非僅曰文辭已也，願熟聞而思之。戒月說戒月說予過吳門之堯峰，戒月禪人以字號求予說，予曰：「戒如瓔珞珠，亦如淨滿月，珠月本圓明，古聖如是說。」然而戒有時而破滅，月終不可滅；月有時

Occurrences.Kwic: 去，始知為道骨瘦如柴，面皮似蠟，喫瓔珞粥一段苦心。然以根器不同，機能各別，所以上士一了一切了，中下多聞多不信。果是英俊道流，自然迥別，咬牙礪齒，嘯傲天真，鼓腹謳歌，遊行自在。大眾！是事且置，只如迦文世尊還墮迷悟也無？千峰勢到嶽邊止，萬派聲歸海上消。」上堂。僧問：「大悲勝相，今日親瞻，無上妙旨，請師指示。」師云：「通身劍戟通身用。」進云：「大悲千手眼，那個是正眼？」師云：「一毫端上定乾坤。」僧擬議，師便喝，乃云：「多載因留意，今朝試為分，此方真教體，清淨在音聞。所以云：『欲識佛性義，當觀時節因緣。』且道今日是什麼時節？」豎拂云：「見麼？即今大士八萬四千母陀羅臂、清淨寶目總向一毫端上一時揭露，一一毫端放無盡光，睹此光者咸超極果。眾中還有未證據者麼？聽取一偈：同結良因正此時，母陀臂展接群機，克期取證無生力，信有功能不浪施。」下座。觀音誕日，上堂。師云：「柳眼舒金，咸是菩薩境界；梅煙粉席，盡屬古佛家風。若是昔有靈骨、具大根器者，一聞所舉，直下無疑，信得及去，坐斷聖凡，了無向背，超情離見，迥絕遮攔，

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J33/J33nB286.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Yingningjing. Yingning Zhijing speaks the full line after striking the whisk and asking the assembly whether they hear.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J36/J36nB359.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Baiyu. Baiyu Jingsi speaks the full line while striking the incense table after sounding a bell image.

Occurrences.Kwic: 夢話人人會說，人人亦曉得該破。至於我們據曲彔床替人做師家底，縱說得來，不過少一箇漁鼓筒，便是唱勸世文底瞎子，有甚麼尊貴說夢？既非尊貴，叫他入理深談，他又全身落在夢中，須知好生慚愧，還敢去開大口？山僧今日與諸公結般若之緣，且不必舉燈籠沿壁上、天台扇子𨁝跳等話，又不必因黎似仲為陳孺人資薦之請，便說漸源生也不道、死也不道底公案，只與諸公就現前實地上輕輕提起，或可向者裏討得一點入路。此道不分在家、出家，但見得真，便受用得，那箇不從說話邊入？所謂此方真教體，清淨在音聞。」以拂子擊案，云：「大眾！還聞麼？者箇是昭昭靈靈底，切不可認他因聲而顯，聲歇時他亦隱沒。如今人耳朵裏聞得有道可學，不愁不多，只愁消不得者要學底心，所以說威音王已前無佛名、無眾生名，斯時正是道。最怕你於總沒有一點事處有箇明明白白之見，此見即同於因聲而起者無有差別，你不要因聲便將心計度云：『我聞底是性了。』大眾！聞底是你性，知到聞底早不是性，乃至二六時中折旋俯仰、口談名理、心計家緣，種種作為事有斷續，而所以為事者無有斷續。你若在萬斷萬續之
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J38/J38nB408.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Aziwa of Haichuang. Azi Jinwu invokes the full line in his own address, strikes the desk, and warns against identifying hearing with a sound that comes and goes.

Senses.Explanation: "In this realm, the true medium of the teaching is sound and hearing in their purity" places hearing at the point of instruction. The masters cite the inherited line and often sound a present object before their listeners. Baichi invokes the line while reflecting on hearing; Zhiyan speaks it in his own hall address. Yingning strikes a whisk and asks whether the assembly hears; Baiyu strikes the incense table. Azi strikes the desk and warns that hearing should not be reduced to a passing sound.

Entries.SourceTerm: 此是心機意識著述得成，待某甲親自勘過

Senses.PreferredTarget: This could be composed through mental contrivance and conscious thought; let me test him myself.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (T/T47/T47n1989.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Lingyou of Weishan, Tanzhou. In the Recorded Sayings of Guishan, Xiangyan has composed a verse after hearing a fragment of tile strike bamboo. Guishan praises his realization, but Yangshan Huiji tells Guishan that such a composition could still have been made through mental contrivance and conscious thought, and asks to examine Xiangyan personally. The headword is Yangshan's reservation and proposal, not Guishan's verdict. During the subsequent examination, Yangshan treats the first verse as something remembered from learning and asks for more. A verse on poverty earns permission for the Tathagata's Zen but not yet the ancestors' Zen; another verse finally brings his acceptance. These are stages of this recorded recognition test: verbal accomplishment is not sufficient for Yangshan until he has tested its speaker. The wording expresses a possibility that the verse was conceptually composed; it does not establish that Xiangyan's realization was false.

得此語？
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J40/J40nB494.xml). Recorded Sayings of Monk Yushan. In Yushan Shangsi's Recorded Sayings, Yushan raises the whole encounter, including Yangshan's exact reservation and the later tests, and then criticizes it before his own assembly. He calls Yangshan's talk dreaming in broad daylight and reproaches Guishan for following his movements instead of correcting him. He describes the ancestral road as full of pits and mounds that he must clear so his listeners can advance. Turning to a contemporary lineage brother named Zunan, he says that neither the Tathagata's Zen nor the ancestors' Zen has any use in that brother's situation. After asking for a sentence expressing a shared road with different tracks, he concludes with Tianning explaining Zen and Fulong expounding precepts, calling the two a contest with two fine colors. The headword remains Yangshan's quoted speech; Yushan is the present critic. His address actively disputes the recognition test rather than furnishing another copy of it. The compressed final comparison is retained without assigning a hidden doctrinal scheme to it.

Occurrences.Kwic: 。西蜀敘州府朱提山朝陽洞月明池和尚傳西蜀敘州府朱提山朝陽洞月明池和尚傳僰道古戎朝陽老人，本郡范氏子，司馬公之後也。幼居林下。一日，有僧過訪不遇，因題聯于壁曰：「阿彌陀佛，閒也念，忙也念，念得佛也無，念也無，無也無，扭落鼻孔；最上乘禪，朝亦參，暮亦參，參到禪亦寂，參亦寂，寂亦寂，劈開面門。」老人見之，忽然厭世，便祝髮就之，彼僧已他往矣。老人遂孤雲白下，飢寒暑濕，憔悴萬狀，單以是聯為提撕話頭。久之，洛伽山路逢一僧，偉儀殊貌，迥出眾表。老人在前行，失腳跌地，念阿彌陀佛。僧在後云：「此是敲門瓦子，何不拋卻？」老人遂參禮云：「拋卻瓦子後如何？」僧云：「葉落歸根，來時無口。」老人遂有省。發睹洛伽畢，復迤邐少林，隨行三十餘眾。值彼旱蝗枯槁，雨如珠玉，食如須陀。眾造無言宗主室，暫欲無言為粥飯，主人乃排坐階下。無言隔窗視之，謂典座曰：「看釜中有粟粥，均給餘眾。殿後坐者，候渠等出，然後以我粥與之。」是時殿後坐者即老人也。老人因是得造室中，與無言論話終日，無言深可之。未幾，辭入關中，過秦嶺，見一頭陀僧，身披紅布褲，頂笠揮鋤地中。老人曰：「者漢好似一頭軍。」僧即云：「看箭。」老人作躲箭勢。僧
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J29/J29nB239.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Chuiwan. The biography of the Chaoyang elder Yue Mingchi recounts his lonely pilgrimage after taking a couplet as his guiding practice. On the road to Luojia he stumbles and calls the Buddha's name. An imposing but unnamed monk behind him says, 'This is a tile for knocking at the door; why not throw it away?' The elder asks what comes after discarding the tile; the monk answers, 'Leaves fall and return to their root; when coming, there is no mouth.' The elder then has an insight. The exact imperative belongs to the unnamed road monk, not the pilgrim or the collection's named master. The tile makes the recited name a means of gaining entry, and the follow-up challenges attachment even to that means. Nothing in this passage identifies the stranger or licenses a general ban on recitation.

Senses.Explanation: This is a tile for knocking at the door; why not throw it away? The biography of the Chaoyang elder Yue Mingchi recounts his lonely pilgrimage after taking a couplet as his guiding practice. On the road to Luojia he stumbles and calls the Buddha's name. An imposing but unnamed monk behind him says, 'This is a tile for knocking at the door; why not throw it away?' The elder asks what comes after discarding the tile; the monk answers, 'Leaves fall and return to their root; when coming, there is no mouth.' The elder then has an insight. The exact imperative belongs to the unnamed road monk, not the pilgrim or the collection's named master. The tile makes the recited name a means of gaining entry, and the follow-up challenges attachment even to that means. Nothing in this passage identifies the stranger or licenses a general ban on recitation. Yeyun Ying retells the same Luojia encounter in his lineage verse collection, retaining the anonymous monk's imperative and the elder's question. That historical quotation remains the old monk's voice. Yeyun then adds his own verse: 'The sound of reciting the Buddha, a door-knocking tile: promptly throw it away, truly free and easy.' He repeats that ease and depicts the elder hidden at Chaoyang, with mind, Buddha and beings thrown into one mixed heap. This is a current poetic interpretation of the very image and discarding action, rather than a second historical meeting. Yeyun's verse supplies the distinct later use; the copied biography itself is not counted twice. Its exuberant ending is poetic praise of relinquishment, not proof that the anonymous monk had a particular canonical identity.

Occurrences.Kwic: 上堂：實是無事，諸人各各是佛，更有何疑得到這裏？古人道：十方同聚會，個個學無為。此是選佛場，心空及第歸。且作麼生是心空？不是那裏閉目冷坐是心空，此正是意識想解。上座要會心空麼？但識自心，便見心空。所以道：過去已過去，未來更莫筭。兀然無事坐，何曾有人喚？設有人喚，上座應他好，不應他好？若應他，阿誰喚上座？若不應他，又不患聾也。三世體空，且不是木頭也。所以古人道：心空得見法王。還見法王麼？也祇是老病僧，又莫道渠自代好。珍重！

Occurrences.Kwic: 結夏，小參。明當結制，今夜小參，舉一兩則古人機緣與諸人商量，非惟截斷葛藤，要且顯出各人自己參學眼目。龐居士云：十方同聚會，箇箇學無為，此是選佛場，心空及第歸。龐居士也甚奇怪，只是俗氣未除。既是心空，歸向什麼處去？無為又作麼生學？然則一言易出，駟馬難追，若是德山、臨濟門下，棒折也未放過在。所以山僧尋常與諸人道：一切處不明，面前有物。直得觸目無滯，達得一切法空，正是面前去不盡底。又不見雲門大師道：平地上死人無數，過得荊棘林是好手。與麼說話，大似將胡猻繫在露柱，有甚快活？既出得荊棘林，又須入得荊棘林始得，所謂入林不動草，入水不動波，然後縱橫得妙，左右逢源，轉地回天，方有自由分。只如者僧道：與麼則堂中上座有長處也。且道：是出耶？是入耶？雲門云：蘇嚧蘇嚧。也是折錐探地。明眼漢到者裏，若作佛法商量，正是平地死人；不作佛法商量，坐在荊棘林裏，三千里賣却布單，特為此事而來，何曾夢見十方聚會？選佛場開，長期百二十日，諸人若善參詳，明取生佛未具已前透頂透底，便是沒量漢也。阿呵呵，也大奇，搖扇取凉，伸脚打睡，三萬六千日，自倒還自起。咄！咄！咄！

Occurrences.Kwic: 結冬，上堂。師云：「神鼎今朝結制，漫天大雪紛飛，不是嚴寒徹骨，那知滴水滴珠？更有艾家翁婆子，專誠慕道遠求師，四百里來請法設齋，供佛供驢。且問諸人：供佛供僧是人知有功德，為什麼卻供驢去？還有委悉者麼？」問：「十方同聚會，箇箇學無為，只如無為作麼生學？」師云：「刺腦入膠盆。」進云：「此是選佛場，心空及第歸。如何是心空及第？」師云：「髑髏粉碎重喫棒。」僧又進語，師以拄杖挃退，云：「看取前話。」乃云：「未結制前，一任諸人喫茶救渴、忍屎抵饑；既結制後，水長船高、泥多佛大。正當今日，卻在已結未結之際，時亨道泰，雨順風調，鼓腹謳歌，萬民樂業。若道山僧上堂開示佛法，山僧留取兩片皮喫飯；若道山僧了無一句開示于人，正是虛生浪死漢子。且道畢竟如何？三文大光錢，買得箇餈粑，高廣八萬由旬，硬如銕、黑似煤，汝等諸人要推推不開、要吞吞不下，神鼎略施方便，便見瓦解冰消。」卓拄杖，喝一喝，云：「不向雲雷超巨浪，終落溝潭網底魚。」

Senses.Explanation: The couplet calls the gathering a buddha-selection ground and says that one whose mind is empty passes the examination and returns. Masters quote it in seasonal assemblies, question its “mind empty,” and compare the gathering to an examination ground. Tian'an Sheng recites the complete four-line verse in his own evening address before naming the figures around the selection ground. Miyun Yuanwu introduces the inherited verse with “therefore it is said” while pointing with his staff, making him the later quoter in this hall address.

Entries.SourceTerm: 此時若不究根源，直待當來問彌勒

Senses.PreferredTarget: If you do not investigate the root now, you will have to wait to ask Maitreya when he comes
AlternateTargets: Fail to seek the root now, and you may as well ask Maitreya in the future
SearchAliases: investigate the root now ask Maitreya later
Senses.Note: The saying urges inquiry into the root now, warning that waiting until the future coming of Maitreya is too late. Four masters speak it as their own present exhortation.

Senses.Explanation: "If you do not investigate the root now, you will have to wait to ask Maitreya when he comes" presses the student to inquire in this very encounter. The four masters use the future Maitreya as an image of delay. Wanru ends an evening address with the warning; Guantao raises his fist before speaking it. Dafang urges complete trust before the line; Yushan shouts and then uses it to close his address.

Entries.SourceTerm: 此藥亦能殺人，亦能活人

Senses.PreferredTarget: This medicine can kill; it can also bring to life
AlternateTargets: The same remedy may kill or revive
SearchAliases: medicine can kill and also heal
same remedy may kill or revive
Senses.Note: In the old encounter, Sudhana finds no plant that is not a medicine, picks up one herb, and hands it to Manjushri, who gives this double verdict. The Chan records use the herb to ask who can apply a teaching and with what effect. Yun’e speaks of direct handling, Miyin warns about using medicine without knowing its effect, Gusu asks what illness is being treated, Weilin asks what to do for someone without illness, and Cishou lifts a whisk as his own remedy. Killing and reviving are the case’s sharp images for the consequences of handling a teaching.

Occurrences.Kwic: 善樂施，去年七十五歲垂誡子孫，一一分明，翛然化去，其信進之力葢可知矣。茲當小祥，其子正謨等特遵遺命上鼓山飯僧，請山僧陞座，也要討箇阿爹本命元辰下落。古者道：紅輪決定沉西去，未委靈魂往那方？須知滔天白浪著力者能有幾人？充國黃金拈出底始是好手。還委悉麼？年年九月九，徧地菊花香。西隱寺僧頓超同善友鄭茂衡、林天章等放生掩骼，滿懺飯僧，請上堂。徧野髑髏，高唱無生之曲；臨危物命，全提殺活之機。子產固所未知，文王亦復未見，却被福城眾多師僧善友一肩領荷。既領荷已，乃復上鼓山，炊無米飯，煑不濕羮，普供大眾，仍請山僧下一轉語，用申慶讚。且道下什麼語即得？要知麼？天下太平，同躋仁壽。文之上座請上堂。秋風凉，秋夜長，未歸客，思故鄉。拍禪床，云：這裏是什麼所在？大家總在裏許，切忌開眼尿床。復舉：文殊菩薩一日令善財採藥，曰：是藥者採將來。善財徧觀大地無不是藥，却來白曰：無有不是藥者。文殊曰：是藥者採將來。善財乃于地上拈一莖草度與文殊，文殊接得呈起，示眾曰：此藥亦能殺人，亦能活人。師云：盡大地是病，盡大地是藥，以如是藥治如是病，無欠無餘，自然恰好。善財可謂善採，文殊可謂善用，若有服之者，直令佛法禪道人我貢高，是非憎愛諸病頓起，通身慶快，許渠作箇洒落底衲僧。雖然，也只醫得箇有病的，忽遇箇無病的來作麼生醫？莫將無事為無事，往往事從無事生。師到南山，二勝和尚請上堂。賣松風於臘月，煞不知時；撾布鼓于雷門，尤堪捧腹。雖然，祇得將錯就錯，向虗空裏打箇筋斗，貴得主賓道合，正脉流通。拈拄杖，云：滿口道不出，信手拈得來。卓一卓，云：瞎驢正法眼，滅却又重開。開後如何？良久，云：不是我堂頭道兄，和尚誰共相委？又卓一卓，下座。師到上生寺，淨悟耆德同信士朱繼禧、劉信篤、葉子珍等設齋，請上堂。師陞座，拈香云：此一瓣香供養妙應和尚。復拈香云：此一瓣香供養曹山寂祖。伏願竈花再發，覺苑重春，駕寶筏于迷津，扇真風于末運。就座云：妙應和尚、曹山寂祖兩箇老古錐，無端向這一片地上撞出頭來，一人為兄在國歡搖頭，一人為弟在上生擺尾，攪渾世界，反覆陰陽，仔細檢點來，猶是冬行春令。山僧為寂祖脚下兒孫，今日到來，雖則祖翁家業契券分明，要且未敢顧著。何也？孟春猶寒，伏惟珍重。泉州開元寺職事石航達際思聖宅出，諸上座送師還山。設齋，請上堂。圓同太虗，無欠無

ClaimAnchors.Kwic: 善樂施，去年七十五歲垂誡子孫，一一分明，翛然化去，其信進之力葢可知矣。茲當小祥，其子正謨等特遵遺命上鼓山飯僧，請山僧陞座，也要討箇阿爹本命元辰下落。古者道：紅輪決定沉西去，未委靈魂往那方？須知滔天白浪著力者能有幾人？充國黃金拈出底始是好手。還委悉麼？年年九月九，徧地菊花香。西隱寺僧頓超同善友鄭茂衡、林天章等放生掩骼，滿懺飯僧，請上堂。徧野髑髏，高唱無生之曲；臨危物命，全提殺活之機。子產固所未知，文王亦復未見，却被福城眾多師僧善友一肩領荷。既領荷已，乃復上鼓山，炊無米飯，煑不濕羮，普供大眾，仍請山僧下一轉語，用申慶讚。且道下什麼語即得？要知麼？天下太平，同躋仁壽。文之上座請上堂。秋風凉，秋夜長，未歸客，思故鄉。拍禪床，云：這裏是什麼所在？大家總在裏許，切忌開眼尿床。復舉：文殊菩薩一日令善財採藥，曰：是藥者採將來。善財徧觀大地無不是藥，却來白曰：無有不是藥者。文殊曰：是藥者採將來。善財乃于地上拈一莖草度與文殊，文殊接得呈起，示眾曰：此藥亦能殺人，亦能活人。師云：盡大地是病，盡大地是藥，以如是藥治如是病，無欠無餘，自然恰好。善財可謂善採，文殊可謂善用，若有服之者，直令佛法禪道人我貢高，是非憎愛諸病頓起，通身慶快，許渠作箇洒落底衲僧。雖然，也只醫得箇有病的，忽遇箇無病的來作麼生醫？莫將無事為無事，往往事從無事生。師到南山，二勝和尚請上堂。賣松風於臘月，煞不知時；撾布鼓于雷門，尤堪捧腹。雖然，祇得將錯就錯，向虗空裏打箇筋斗，貴得主賓道合，正脉流通。拈拄杖，云：滿口道不出，信手拈得來。卓一卓，云：瞎驢正法眼，滅却又重開。開後如何？良久，云：不是我堂頭道兄，和尚誰共相委？又卓一卓，下座。師到上生寺，淨悟耆德同信士朱繼禧、劉信篤、葉子珍等設齋，請上堂。師陞座，拈香云：此一瓣香供養妙應和尚。復拈香云：此一瓣香供養曹山寂祖。伏願竈花再發，覺苑重春，駕寶筏于迷津，扇真風于末運。就座云：妙應和尚、曹山寂祖兩箇老古錐，無端向這一片地上撞出頭來，一人為兄在國歡搖頭，一人為弟在上生擺尾，攪渾世界，反覆陰陽，仔細檢點來，猶是冬行春令。山僧為寂祖脚下兒孫，今日到來，雖則祖翁家業契券分明，要且未敢顧著。何也？孟春猶寒，伏惟珍重。泉州開元寺職事石航達際思聖宅出，諸上座送師還山。設齋，請上堂。圓同太虗，無欠無

Senses.Explanation: The same herb can harm or help; the question is who knows how to use it. Yun’e tests direct handling, while Miyin warns that a remedy without knowledge of its use can turn harmful. Gusu asks about the illness, Weilin asks about a person with none, and Cishou raises his whisk as a fresh medicine.

Senses.PreferredTarget: This medicine can kill a person, and it can bring a person to life
AlternateTargets: This remedy can both kill and revive
SearchAliases: medicine can kill person bring person to life
Senses.Note: The saying is attributed to Manjushri when he receives a stalk of grass from Sudhana. Later masters test the exchange and the relation of disease and remedy; the plant is not identified and no practical medical claim is established.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J38/J38nB407.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Shengren of Qianshan. Hanke raises the exchange in full: Sudhana first reports that nothing is not medicine, then, after Manjushri repeats the request, hands him a stalk of grass. Manjushri's statement is the headword. Hanke raises his whisk and offers a figurative medicine unknown to the legendary physicians, then asks whether it is the same as Manjushri's. Repeating the headword as Manjushri's words, he contrasts his own remedy, which permits neither seeking life nor seeking death. He goes on to distinguish bodily illnesses from successive diseases of attachment, finally asks who can prescribe for his own disease, and includes Manjushri and Sudhana in the scrutiny. The inherited statement and Hanke's deliberately escalating medicine imagery are separate voices.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J29/J29nB234.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Yichuyuan. In Yichu's series of verses on old cases, Sudhana's broad report that everything is medicine is followed by Manjushri's repeated demand and the offering of one blade of grass. Manjushri receives it, shows it to the assembly, and gives the headword. Yichu's four-line verse then warns against wrongly circulating the medicine's nature. It asks whose power is responsible for killing and reviving and directs attention to the point before Manjushri raised it. The headword is the quoted figure's speech; the warning and question are Yichu's response, not a claim about the chemical properties of a particular herb. The next unit concerns Manjushri being confined between iron mountains.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J37/J37nB396.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Zisu of Panlong, Zhongnan Mountain. Zisu recounts Sudhana's search, the report that nothing is not medicine, and Manjushri's receipt of the grass and declaration. Zisu says Manjushri may be able to fool Sudhana, but he would answer the claim to kill and revive by asking how thick his skin is, then watch how he proceeds. This is Zisu's proposed challenge, not a reply recorded as actually given by Sudhana. The headword belongs to Manjushri's original quoted statement; the current commentary tests the authority of that statement rather than merely endorsing the grass as a universal remedy. The next case is Zhaozhou's seven-pound robe.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J39/J39nB452.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Lüyan He. Luyan raises the complete exchange and then comments on both participants. Sudhana has turned earth into gold, he says, yet is already covered in mud; Manjushri displays killing and reviving fully, but has a dragon's head and a snake's tail. Luyan would intervene earlier: on hearing Sudhana say that nothing is not medicine, he would strike him across the back. His final explanation is cast in an image of drawing a sword. The headword remains Manjushri's quoted declaration; the proposed blow belongs to Luyan's alternative handling and is directed at Sudhana's general answer, before the grass is handed over.

Senses.Explanation: Manjushri asks Sudhana to bring medicine. Sudhana sees nothing that is not medicine, but Manjushri repeats the request until he brings a stalk of grass. Manjushri holds it up and says that this medicine can kill and can bring to life. The contrast is part of a teaching case, not medical advice about an identified plant. Later comments do not simply affirm that every object is a useful remedy. Hanke presents his own figurative medicine and keeps asking who will treat the remaining disease; Yichu's verse asks whose power kills and revives and points before Manjushri raises the grass. Zisu would challenge Manjushri's claim directly, while Luyan would strike at Sudhana's earlier general answer. The notes distinguish the original grass-taking exchange, the repeated quotation, and each present master's criticism or imagined intervention. Their differing moves matter more than treating killing and reviving as a fixed property of the grass.

Baiyun Shouduan owns the retained dare: Mahakasyapa's eyes, Anguilimala's stripes, Mudgalyana's feet crossing the pit, Mahakasyapa the elder dancing to the zither, Pilingkajie cursing the river spirit, Kalingudayin buried in dung — each has its warrant in the teaching; and at the gate of the founder: nine years facing the wall, Bimo's staff, Heshan's drum, Shigong's bow, Xuefeng's ball, the National Master's water bowl, Guizong dragging stone, Deshan's staff at the door, Linji's shout at the door, Wuye's 'give up deluded thinking' — say, what is this? is there in the throng one long-trained worthy who walks crosswise under heaven with an eye above the crown of his head? come out and stand witness for Baiyun, and give this life one free breath — anyone? anyone? if not — thirty years on, this saying will travel — and how, in the end? the summer's fire-clouds return to the blue cave; clear autumn's perilous dew drips on the golden plate.

Wansong Xingxiu owns the retained gloss: the Mao ode 'Qiyu' praises the Duke of Wu — a man of letters who could still hear remonstrance, guarding himself by ritual, hence rising to minister at Zhou; cut bone, file ivory, carve jade, grind stone — Deshan's Xuefeng won his final word from Yantou, and to this day this saying travels: the power of cutting and grinding, of turning and changing; Xuefeng is the staff that turns into a dragon, that monk the shuttle still coiled in its cocoon; Yantou pointed it out and to this day no one knows — hence 'dying on the same branch' has few.

Gulin Qingmao owns the retained verdict: Zhuyu held up a peg of bamboo in the hall — can anyone drive a peg into empty space? — elder Lingxu came out: empty space is the peg — Zhuyu struck him; do not strike me in error — and Zhuyu let it rest; Xuedou's verdict: to make this saying travel, you must finish the strikes and chase him out; the master's own: to make this saying travel, you must drive the peg into empty space — and if some fellow comes out and says 'empty space is the peg,' how do you answer? a horse run on ice-edges, a body turned on the sword-blade — that is my everyday use; let it pass, and where would this crew of sleepers grope? — and he drove them all out with a flurry of the staff.

Liangting Jingting owns the retained tea-talk: the clouds and the moon are the same, the streams and the hills each differ — back then Jiashan and Luopu cut off the tongue, this saying traveled, and so this day came to be; today the stream and moon are wholly the same, the clouds and hills not different: brows level, nose straight, the swan white, the crow black; come from Tiantai heading to Jingshan, all together walk into Xixi, by the misty-water road enter the gate of the towered pavilion, and pass the river islet without escape — the whale swallows the sea and bares the coral; let Jiashan's Boatman, Nanyue and Qingyuan, all the old augers from the beginning, be drawn by one rope to that side — a fair share of freedom and ease.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J39/J39nB454.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Pinjixiang. Pinjixiang Zhixiang owns the retained stamp: asked — a lifespan beyond dust-aeons, please point it out — the winter plum on the ridge is just baring its jade; then the whole great earth shares the moistening — Muzhou only carries the board; Nanquan is used to selling himself; heaven and earth one root — there really is the way! — and the master: thirty years on, this saying will travel — then, to the hall: the affair under the founders demands you sweat out a whole white sweat before you know the descending pure wind; though Yangshan said it cannot be said, he only watched heaven tip in the southeast and never saw earth notch in the northwest; and even one who could say it is not allowed to sit with Chen of Muzhou and old teacher Wang — to know the meaning of a lifespan beyond dust-aeons, wait straight until thirty years on, when someone will raise it of himself.

Senses.Explanation: This saying will travel: a supplied answer, a dare to the silent hall, a price put on a word thirty years out. Yunmen Wenyan, over a case already closed in silence: a monk leaving Shishuang Qingzhu — by boat or by land? — meet a boat, take the boat; meet land, take the land — I say the halfway point is rather hard — no words; and the master supplied: thirty years on, this saying will travel — one line at parting, unforgotten for a whole aeon. Baiyun Shouduan, after the founders' roll-call — the wall-facing nine years, the staff, the drum, the bow, the ball, the water bowl, the dragged stone, the shout at the door — say, what is this? is there one who walks crosswise under heaven with an eye above his crown? come out and stand witness for Baiyun; anyone? anyone? if not — thirty years on, this saying will travel. Wansong Xingxiu, glossing the cutting-polishing ode: Deshan's Xuefeng won his final word from Yantou, and to this day this saying travels — the power of cutting and grinding; Xuefeng is the staff that turns into a dragon, that monk the shuttle still coiled; Yantou pointed it out and no one to this day knows. Gulin Qingmao, over the peg in empty space: Zhuyu held up the bamboo peg; elder Lingxu said empty space is the peg and took the strike; Xuedou's verdict — finish the strikes and chase him out; the master's own — to make this saying travel, drive the peg into empty space; and if someone says 'empty space is the peg,' how do you answer? — a horse on the ice-edges, a body turned on the sword-blade; let it pass, and where would the sleepers grope? Nanyuan Huiyong, carried in Sanfeng's genealogy: a monk from Xiangzhou come specially to bow — you have just missed the old man of Baoying, he is not in — a shout; I told you he is not in — another shout, and the staff; the monk bowed: this staff was by rights yours to strike me — I strike you with it instead — this saying must travel — blind man, off to the hall! Liangting Jingting, over tea: the clouds and the moon are the same, the streams and hills each differ — back then Jiashan and Luopu cut off the tongue, this saying traveled, and so this day came to be; today brows level, nose straight, the swan white, the crow black — and let all the old augers from Jiashan's Boatman to Nanyue and Qingyuan be drawn by one rope to that side. Pinjixiang Zhixiang, on the heaven-earth-one-root exchange: a lifespan beyond dust-aeons — the winter plum just baring its jade; the whole earth shares the moistening — Muzhou only carries the board, Nanquan is used to selling himself — heaven and earth one root, there really is the way! — and the master: thirty years on, this saying will travel — and it demands a whole white sweat of you; even one who could say it is not allowed to sit with Chen of Muzhou and old teacher Wang; wait thirty years, and someone will raise it of himself.

Entries.SourceTerm: 此身不向今生度，更向何生度此身

Senses.PreferredTarget: If this body is not freed in this life, in what life will it be freed?
SearchAliases: If this body is not freed in this life, in what life will it be freed?
Senses.Note: The question presses the practitioner to act in this life. It does not promise automatic release through urgency alone.

Occurrences.Kwic: 也。長人勉之。復張一生居士復張一生居士讀來札，知居士於病冗中不昧正念，喜慰！喜慰！但所云「凡百綢錯都非本領而生厭苦」者，此固學道人初心通病，第未審居士以何為本領耳？學道若不經惡逆境緣烹煉，終是照覺不出，雖云毫無進步，不妨舉覺分明。若有能覺、所覺之異，則有覺痛、痛覺之殊；若能虛照無緣，則病業與身俱如雲影矣。病與不病既不可得，而知搜討無落處者誰乎？何不并那怕落空底亦空，即此空亦不可得？如是，則十方世界廓落目前，藥罐爐邊超凡入聖。雖然如是，後日相見，若守此作解，一棒打折汝腰，莫言不道。又禪者冒暑遠迎，足見賢契輩信心真切，但神鼎一時不能撒手，且其地僻山深，似非老祖菩提之可及，不大不小，可暫可長。今來狐鼠望風歸，正俟年熟世平，料理就緒，移風易俗，未可知也。但所慮者，一生雖於此道有望見處，而理不勝情，苟未向天真未判已前迎刃而解，并解亦忘，鮮有不為情識所推移者，惟願一生勉之。玄沙云：「今時人不悟箇中道理相，自涉塵涉事，頭頭羈絆。縱悟，則塵境紛紜，名相不實，一生雖數年聚首，而實未到卒地折、爆地斷，不免坐在無為無事蘊界中。臘月三十到來，恐卒著手腳不便，天地如幻，百年如夢，更有什麼心情閑處用？」古人所謂：此身不向今生度，更向何生度此身？好言語，只恐一生錯會耳。如今一彈指悟去，萬劫千生只如是，如是二字不得動著，動著打折汝驢腰。一生還會麼？遮裏會去，五年指示，了無實義。雖無實義，法法全該，非是強為，法如是故。如或未能全提得去，仍須看山僧所示開口也打、不開口也打話，二六時中緊著精神，不得絲毫走作，稍有依通解會現前，急忙掃向他方世界。如是廝挨將去，自然六窗虛靜，萬慮安閑，事事頭頭省無限力，省無限力處便是得力時也。相晤之期，未知何日？不辭縷縷。寄金正希太史寄金正希太史前冬久擾香積，別後又承施問，而不一致書稱謝者，以居士之不必謝，而亦無飛鴻之便也。客冬始得入匡廬晤大中兄，知居士於天童老人處盤桓十許日，不審邇來礙膺之物得脫落無滯否？若果到此，切莫便休，但盡妄情，別無生死可得。何謂妄情？日用應酬有箇主宰執著者是。能所纔生，則是非、凡聖、愛憎、取捨種種心識，如鉤鎖連環，相續不斷，是為生死。若能了知自心本非有無，則能所不立，終日應緣，全無滯礙，何處有生死得來？縱有餘習未淨，只須退步返觀，當下冰消瓦解，不知居士有當於心否？如或覺明未化，見浪仍馳，須看古人無義味話，念念在中，心心無間，逼到計窮力盡，大地回春，送向聲色堆中自由自在，方可喫山

Occurrences.Kwic: 門。如今居士之稱，莫作等閑看了。既稱居士，要與維摩一樣行事，方稱居士。既擔當居士名號，不見僧家之過，是名真維摩也。過去者是古居士，現在者是新維摩耳。真正護法人，不見三寶過。護惜三寶者，如護眼中之珠，是名活韋馱也，亦名護法諸天菩薩。古德云：『天、人、阿修羅，皆歸第一義。』要汝等斬新條令，回向三寶，永不退轉。皈依佛法僧，不是教汝等皈依有相佛，即相離相，離相見佛，一體三身。三身者何？法身者，是汝等自己清淨佛也；報身者，是汝等色身佛也；化身者，是汝等妙用神通自在佛也，亦名千百億化身釋迦牟尼佛。山僧與汝等下個註腳，能淨即釋迦，慈悲即觀音，喜捨即勢至，直心是彌陀，平等即彌勒，能說即文殊，能行即普賢。《法華》云：『開佛知見，示佛知見，悟佛知見，入佛知見』耳。開示汝等悟入無生法忍，所以種種言辭、種種譬喻，說三車在門外，令汝等快出三界塵勞，永離諸苦，證安樂境界，獨證真常，恒不退轉。種種布施、種種供養、種種莊嚴、種種如意，唯會一乘之道，成正等覺，與諸佛、諸祖、諸大善知識、古今尊宿，同一眼見，同一耳聞，同一鼻孔出氣，把臂共行，要汝等知過必改，得能莫忘。人身難得，中國難生，善知識難遇，佛法難聞。黃龍禪師云：『此身不向今生度，更向何生度此身？八十翁翁入場屋，真誠不是小兒戲。』努力，努力！至囑，至囑！山僧坐視不禁，只得搖唇鼓舌，一片婆心，牽枝引蔓，不覺葛藤滿地，一場漏逗。忽有個傍不肯的出來，拽下禪床，痛搥一頓：『這裏是甚麼所在？說心說性，說黃道白。』山僧與他結個同參，云：『感恩不盡。』把手牽君行不得，惟人自肯乃方親。」大方禪師禪燈語錄卷一終禪燈菴大方禪師語錄卷二嗣法門人超鳴編拈頌拈頌世尊初生。「世尊眼空四海，可謂旁若無人；雲門令行千古，未免傷鋒犯手。這二老為人，一個向高高山頂立，一個向深深海底行，看來也是同坑無異土。」四顧周行全體彰，大方獨步勢無雙，雲門一棒掀天地，千古兒孫任舉揚。世尊，明星悟道。「世尊夜睹明星，大似開眼作夢，說甚麼妄想執著，證得證不得，何不向明星未出時薦取，何等勦絕，更說甚麼智慧德相，累及後人，牽枝引蔓，葛藤滿地。」抬頭忽覺滿天星，大地眾生豁眼睛，試問當年何所得？和泥合水向人傾。拈華微笑。「世尊拈華，年老心孤；迦葉微笑，知恩有地。檢點將來，二俱不了。海上座當時纔見他舉手處，咄云：『不勞拈出。』免得後代兒孫承虛接響。」一枝拈出大家看，百萬人天盡被瞞，微笑頭陀親薦得，燈燈不絕古今傳。女子出定。「女子無端特地，

Occurrences.Kwic: 你將箇一歸何處晝參夜參，無論閒忙動靜，無論逆順喜怒，遇飯喫飯，遇茶喫茶，孜孜汲汲，切切拳拳，如鐵橛子相似。稍有雜念起時，即舉本參話頭，如金剛王寶劍，直下看這雜念從何處起，咬定牙根，豎起脊梁，工夫自然成片。參到不舉自舉，不提自提，胸次中覺得氣氣悶悶，推之不去，蕩之不散。此際工夫，再不可放手，亦不可執著坐相。如若睡魔起時，便下單抖擻精神，向本參上追究，急切提撕一回，睡魔自然退矣。自要發箇勇猛，千期萬期，以悟為期。若能如是恒常不怠，那怕甕中走卻鱉，此事亦不得性急。你看古人動經十年二十年，揩磨得一點氣息也無，所以得到這般田地。今人切忌草草，光陰易過，時不待人，各自努力。葛藤未盡，更說一偈：『話頭提起利如鋒，犯者從教絕影蹤，劣性初調頻著力，牧童鞭策莫相容。』」警眾。「既為如來弟子，圓頂方袍，必要立向上志，發堅固心，莫辜負佛祖建立垂慈之德，莫辜負國王外護水土之恩，莫辜負父母師長養育剃度之情，莫辜負自己辭親割愛出家之志，莫虛消信施，莫虛度光陰，無常老病，不與人期，轉眼便是來生，莫被閻羅老子索你飯錢，縱有親爺親娘救你不得，縱有相契善友替你不回，閻羅王不怕你口尖舌快，牽入六道四生，悔之晚矣。所以古云：『此身不向今生度，更向何生度此身？』何不趁此色力強健，四大安康，猛烈一番，討箇明曰。今幸處閒居靜室，明淨僧堂，粥飯不缺，茶湯穩便，汝等若不做工夫，真為下劣愚癡漢矣。二六時中，將箇話頭頓在面前，豎起脊梁，開著兩眼，如貓捕鼠，不容走作，念茲在茲，默默參究，須瓣一片恒常不退之志，晝夜無間，逆順一如。汝等秖為看得生死事輕，所以被無明煩惱雜念分飛，障閉悟門，或昏沉散亂，攪作一團，或有頭無尾，中道而止，或參到無滋味處，便要丟手，此乃參禪人最忌之病。若能依我說話，自然有發明日子。珍重。」圓通大士開光。師云：「世間一切有為無不皆從願力而生，這段公案乃義公法兄夢感發心，多緣時節不至、面目未彰，故爾擔閣至今。若非諸檀護出手相扶，妙莊嚴相焉能成就？然而大象無形，云何有相？正是月臨千澗，花發陽春。菩薩三十二應，無剎不現身；善財五十三參，有緣方住足。今日伏獅院裏大士降生了也，且道有何祥瑞？」豎拂，云：「大眾見麼？大士在山僧拂子頭上現百千三昧而為說法，且道說什麼法？不見一法即如來，是則名為觀自在。以是因緣，我先法兄了其宿願，常寂光中得大自在；十方信施發菩提心，各霑法味得大自在；現前大眾耳觀目聽，徹證圓通得大自在。且如何是自在一句？」以拂子點，云

Occurrences.Kwic: 是實？若如此懞懞懂懂，逗到頭白齒黃，忽然一朝，陰境現前，前路茫茫，不知何往，翻思從前所用之心，總如空花電露，始知依稀念佛持咒的心用不得，貪嗔嫉妒的用不得，囫圇參究的用不得，到此始頓足扼腕，追之晚矣。在今法道凋殘，兵戈四起，眾苦交煎，求其與道真實參尋者難得，且近來諸方榜樣大不堪聞，上下依稀，誠為法門大變，況此事不在機鋒言語邊論，不在奇特玄妙中求，須是你打頭遇箇本色師家，不以聲色籠絡，不以知解穿通，只教你力究真參，你便好放下孃生面孔，於十二時中一直參求，如急水灘頭逆風撐舟的相似，一篙了又一篙，篙篙相值、手手相乘，若不到風恬浪穩處，爭敢休歇？必要撐到水寂波澄，布帆穩便的時節，㘞地將從前驚疑怖畏之心一齊放下，撇轉頭來，始見：月明兩岸蘆花白，古渡無人不繫舟。如不得恁麼一回，都是死門。豈不見，圓悟和尚見演祖時，機鋒何等穎捷？祖見即詬罵曰：『佛法大事，豈口頭聲色所至哉？若以機辯為禪，則臘月三十日涅槃堂裏，爭奈孤燈獨照何？』後來圓悟到金山遇一場熱病，始知演祖藥頭靈驗，所以，你諸人參須真參，悟須實悟。今既來此，深山窮谷，聚頭不為別事，須是生大慚愧，將自家教不過的一著子心心念念晝參夜究，必期徹證。古云：『此身不向今生度，更向何生度此身？』山僧自來行腳，亦不曾廣參知識、行寡人微，只是守定箇本色，實願於萬山深處與你諸人，同行同坐、同起同眠，只要令汝向懸巖撒手、絕後再甦，此外更沒有別的長處。若論祖師機向上句，山僧拄杖子走遍四天下，竟不曾遇著一箇會佛法的，但只撞倒舜若多神道。邇來鹽豐米貴，官路甚嚴，寄意山頭長老，慎不可冬行春令。久立諸公，伏惟珍重。」普說。「今朝是結制的最初夜，從今已去八十五日，第一要你諸人有箇趣向，若或時中無趣向、無把柄，便名無主孤魂、纏空外道。諸兄弟！道不可以見聞覺知求，亦不可離見聞覺知會。若以見聞覺知求，是認影迷頭，終不見道；若離見聞覺知會，即破波求水，亦無所獲。如是即不得、離不得、離即俱不到，畢竟如何即得？」遂舉如意云：「好向山僧如意子頭上會取。若會得者一著子，不唯知他離即不到，亦知如意子有種種神通、具種種三昧，有時現溈仰身入九十六種三昧，說暗機義海、圓相法門；有時現臨濟身，入總別無礙陀羅尼三昧，說玄要賓主、縱奪料揀等種種法門；有時現雲門身入獅子奮迅三昧，說一字關、六不收、顧鑒咦等種種法門；有時現法眼身入遍一切三昧，說唯心旨訣、六相義等種種法門；只是不現曹洞身，不入重玄三昧，不說正偏王子、功勛滲漏等

ClaimAnchors.Kwic: 門。如今居士之稱，莫作等閑看了。既稱居士，要與維摩一樣行事，方稱居士。既擔當居士名號，不見僧家之過，是名真維摩也。過去者是古居士，現在者是新維摩耳。真正護法人，不見三寶過。護惜三寶者，如護眼中之珠，是名活韋馱也，亦名護法諸天菩薩。古德云：『天、人、阿修羅，皆歸第一義。』要汝等斬新條令，回向三寶，永不退轉。皈依佛法僧，不是教汝等皈依有相佛，即相離相，離相見佛，一體三身。三身者何？法身者，是汝等自己清淨佛也；報身者，是汝等色身佛也；化身者，是汝等妙用神通自在佛也，亦名千百億化身釋迦牟尼佛。山僧與汝等下個註腳，能淨即釋迦，慈悲即觀音，喜捨即勢至，直心是彌陀，平等即彌勒，能說即文殊，能行即普賢。《法華》云：『開佛知見，示佛知見，悟佛知見，入佛知見』耳。開示汝等悟入無生法忍，所以種種言辭、種種譬喻，說三車在門外，令汝等快出三界塵勞，永離諸苦，證安樂境界，獨證真常，恒不退轉。種種布施、種種供養、種種莊嚴、種種如意，唯會一乘之道，成正等覺，與諸佛、諸祖、諸大善知識、古今尊宿，同一眼見，同一耳聞，同一鼻孔出氣，把臂共行，要汝等知過必改，得能莫忘。人身難得，中國難生，善知識難遇，佛法難聞。黃龍禪師云：『此身不向今生度，更向何生度此身？八十翁翁入場屋，真誠不是小兒戲。』努力，努力！至囑，至囑！山僧坐視不禁，只得搖唇鼓舌，一片婆心，牽枝引蔓，不覺葛藤滿地，一場漏逗。忽有個傍不肯的出來，拽下禪床，痛搥一頓：『這裏是甚麼所在？說心說性，說黃道白。』山僧與他結個同參，云：『感恩不盡。』把手牽君行不得，惟人自肯乃方親。」大方禪師禪燈語錄卷一終禪燈菴大方禪師語錄卷二嗣法門人超鳴編拈頌拈頌世尊初生。「世尊眼空四海，可謂旁若無人；雲門令行千古，未免傷鋒犯手。這二老為人，一個向高高山頂立，一個向深深海底行，看來也是同坑無異土。」四顧周行全體彰，大方獨步勢無雙，雲門一棒掀天地，千古兒孫任舉揚。世尊，明星悟道。「世尊夜睹明星，大似開眼作夢，說甚麼妄想執著，證得證不得，何不向明星未出時薦取，何等勦絕，更說甚麼智慧德相，累及後人，牽枝引蔓，葛藤滿地。」抬頭忽覺滿天星，大地眾生豁眼睛，試問當年何所得？和泥合水向人傾。拈華微笑。「世尊拈華，年老心孤；迦葉微笑，知恩有地。檢點將來，二俱不了。海上座當時纔見他舉手處，咄云：『不勞拈出。』免得後代兒孫承虛接響。」一枝拈出大家看，百萬人天盡被瞞，微笑頭陀親薦得，燈燈不絕古今傳。女子出定。「女子無端特地，

ClaimAnchors.Kwic: 你將箇一歸何處晝參夜參，無論閒忙動靜，無論逆順喜怒，遇飯喫飯，遇茶喫茶，孜孜汲汲，切切拳拳，如鐵橛子相似。稍有雜念起時，即舉本參話頭，如金剛王寶劍，直下看這雜念從何處起，咬定牙根，豎起脊梁，工夫自然成片。參到不舉自舉，不提自提，胸次中覺得氣氣悶悶，推之不去，蕩之不散。此際工夫，再不可放手，亦不可執著坐相。如若睡魔起時，便下單抖擻精神，向本參上追究，急切提撕一回，睡魔自然退矣。自要發箇勇猛，千期萬期，以悟為期。若能如是恒常不怠，那怕甕中走卻鱉，此事亦不得性急。你看古人動經十年二十年，揩磨得一點氣息也無，所以得到這般田地。今人切忌草草，光陰易過，時不待人，各自努力。葛藤未盡，更說一偈：『話頭提起利如鋒，犯者從教絕影蹤，劣性初調頻著力，牧童鞭策莫相容。』」警眾。「既為如來弟子，圓頂方袍，必要立向上志，發堅固心，莫辜負佛祖建立垂慈之德，莫辜負國王外護水土之恩，莫辜負父母師長養育剃度之情，莫辜負自己辭親割愛出家之志，莫虛消信施，莫虛度光陰，無常老病，不與人期，轉眼便是來生，莫被閻羅老子索你飯錢，縱有親爺親娘救你不得，縱有相契善友替你不回，閻羅王不怕你口尖舌快，牽入六道四生，悔之晚矣。所以古云：『此身不向今生度，更向何生度此身？』何不趁此色力強健，四大安康，猛烈一番，討箇明曰。今幸處閒居靜室，明淨僧堂，粥飯不缺，茶湯穩便，汝等若不做工夫，真為下劣愚癡漢矣。二六時中，將箇話頭頓在面前，豎起脊梁，開著兩眼，如貓捕鼠，不容走作，念茲在茲，默默參究，須瓣一片恒常不退之志，晝夜無間，逆順一如。汝等秖為看得生死事輕，所以被無明煩惱雜念分飛，障閉悟門，或昏沉散亂，攪作一團，或有頭無尾，中道而止，或參到無滋味處，便要丟手，此乃參禪人最忌之病。若能依我說話，自然有發明日子。珍重。」圓通大士開光。師云：「世間一切有為無不皆從願力而生，這段公案乃義公法兄夢感發心，多緣時節不至、面目未彰，故爾擔閣至今。若非諸檀護出手相扶，妙莊嚴相焉能成就？然而大象無形，云何有相？正是月臨千澗，花發陽春。菩薩三十二應，無剎不現身；善財五十三參，有緣方住足。今日伏獅院裏大士降生了也，且道有何祥瑞？」豎拂，云：「大眾見麼？大士在山僧拂子頭上現百千三昧而為說法，且道說什麼法？不見一法即如來，是則名為觀自在。以是因緣，我先法兄了其宿願，常寂光中得大自在；十方信施發菩提心，各霑法味得大自在；現前大眾耳觀目聽，徹證圓通得大自在。且如何是自在一句？」以拂子點，云

ClaimAnchors.Kwic: 是實？若如此懞懞懂懂，逗到頭白齒黃，忽然一朝，陰境現前，前路茫茫，不知何往，翻思從前所用之心，總如空花電露，始知依稀念佛持咒的心用不得，貪嗔嫉妒的用不得，囫圇參究的用不得，到此始頓足扼腕，追之晚矣。在今法道凋殘，兵戈四起，眾苦交煎，求其與道真實參尋者難得，且近來諸方榜樣大不堪聞，上下依稀，誠為法門大變，況此事不在機鋒言語邊論，不在奇特玄妙中求，須是你打頭遇箇本色師家，不以聲色籠絡，不以知解穿通，只教你力究真參，你便好放下孃生面孔，於十二時中一直參求，如急水灘頭逆風撐舟的相似，一篙了又一篙，篙篙相值、手手相乘，若不到風恬浪穩處，爭敢休歇？必要撐到水寂波澄，布帆穩便的時節，㘞地將從前驚疑怖畏之心一齊放下，撇轉頭來，始見：月明兩岸蘆花白，古渡無人不繫舟。如不得恁麼一回，都是死門。豈不見，圓悟和尚見演祖時，機鋒何等穎捷？祖見即詬罵曰：『佛法大事，豈口頭聲色所至哉？若以機辯為禪，則臘月三十日涅槃堂裏，爭奈孤燈獨照何？』後來圓悟到金山遇一場熱病，始知演祖藥頭靈驗，所以，你諸人參須真參，悟須實悟。今既來此，深山窮谷，聚頭不為別事，須是生大慚愧，將自家教不過的一著子心心念念晝參夜究，必期徹證。古云：『此身不向今生度，更向何生度此身？』山僧自來行腳，亦不曾廣參知識、行寡人微，只是守定箇本色，實願於萬山深處與你諸人，同行同坐、同起同眠，只要令汝向懸巖撒手、絕後再甦，此外更沒有別的長處。若論祖師機向上句，山僧拄杖子走遍四天下，竟不曾遇著一箇會佛法的，但只撞倒舜若多神道。邇來鹽豐米貴，官路甚嚴，寄意山頭長老，慎不可冬行春令。久立諸公，伏惟珍重。」普說。「今朝是結制的最初夜，從今已去八十五日，第一要你諸人有箇趣向，若或時中無趣向、無把柄，便名無主孤魂、纏空外道。諸兄弟！道不可以見聞覺知求，亦不可離見聞覺知會。若以見聞覺知求，是認影迷頭，終不見道；若離見聞覺知會，即破波求水，亦無所獲。如是即不得、離不得、離即俱不到，畢竟如何即得？」遂舉如意云：「好向山僧如意子頭上會取。若會得者一著子，不唯知他離即不到，亦知如意子有種種神通、具種種三昧，有時現溈仰身入九十六種三昧，說暗機義海、圓相法門；有時現臨濟身，入總別無礙陀羅尼三昧，說玄要賓主、縱奪料揀等種種法門；有時現雲門身入獅子奮迅三昧，說一字關、六不收、顧鑒咦等種種法門；有時現法眼身入遍一切三昧，說唯心旨訣、六相義等種種法門；只是不現曹洞身，不入重玄三昧，不說正偏王子、功勛滲漏等

Senses.Explanation: A heart laid bare, piece after piece pictures sincerity with nothing held back. Chan speakers use it to acknowledge wholehearted effort while preserving the right to criticize the move that effort produced. Fushan Kou calls Yunmen wholehearted and in the same breath says both Yunmen and Xuedou lack the eye at the crown. Zongben Yuanming turns recognition of such a heart into a hall question; Yulin Tongxiu labels his own severe warning heartfelt despite calling it frost added to snow. Yinyuan Longqi says an old master’s wholeheartedness is fully exposed and raises the whisk to make the claim visible before the assembly.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J26/J26nB188.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Rujiu Ruibai. At his opening assembly, Ruibai Mingxue says this matter is possessed by everyone and manifest everywhere: round, lively and exposed, with nothing leaking away or shielding it. The headword names that unshielded quality beside 'nakedly exposed,' rather than reporting a person removing clothes. Raising his whisk, he tests whether the assembly understands, then reworks Fadeng's old account of coming out to settle his teacher's unfinished case. The description of complete exposure does not make that new test unnecessary; Ruibai still asks the listeners to distinguish his treatment from the old teacher's.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J39/J39nB448.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Lingji. A monk tells Lingji Xingguan that he has traveled countless mountains but still finds awakening through Zhaozhou's cypress difficult. Lingji answers that it is bare directly before his face. The headword counters the apparent distance and difficulty of the monk's search with immediate exposure; it does not supply a literal naked body as the cypress case's answer. Nearby exchanges in the same record rebuke a monk for merely repeating the teacher's phrase and test whether listeners know where their bows land. Those limits matter: saying 'bare before you' is not evidence that the questioner has already understood.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (B/B25/B25n0145.xml). Extensive Record of Zhongfeng Mingben of Tianmu. On the Buddha's awakening day, Zhongfeng Mingben describes the true matter as impossible to name or depict, yet brilliant, round, pure and bare. He then announces Shakyamuni within the listeners' own eyes, seeing the morning star and awakening at their heads. If they do not understand, they must return to their seats and take up their unresolved question energetically. His ensuing prohibitions include neither fighting distraction mechanically nor rejecting imagined thoughts to seek truth, neither seeking holiness nor waiting for awakening. The headword's exposure is part of this current address, not actual undressing or a new historical awakening by the Buddha in that room.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X72/X72n1437.xml). Expanded Record of Chan Master Yongjue Yuanxian. After Tang's gift of a communal bath, Yongjue Yuanxian asks how the monks will repay him. Learned explanations of Bhadrapala's bathing realization are only talk about food, not food that satisfies hunger; even genuine attainment still meets the teacher's further challenge. How can one give a full rather than borrowed or half sentence? His closing verse says to take off the foul undershirt and meet the present person bare, yet warns that without the lion's turning method the mountains and waters remain deep. Literal bathing supports the image, while the qualifier prevents equating removing clothes with completing the teaching.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J25/J25nB171.xml). Recorded Sayings of Monk Tianyin. At the first awakening-day address in the cold huts of Qingshan, Tianyin Yuanxiu describes arrivals who have lost their usual bearings and stand bare without clothes. He immediately asks what the exceptional turning point is, answers with a mud ox drinking from the Wuling stream and raises his whisk as Shakyamuni shining in the listeners' eyelashes. They must see this themselves; otherwise entering the empty gate has been in vain. The headword works as an exposed, unprotected condition within this challenge. It is not a report that arriving monks were physically deprived of robes or a sufficient certificate of their realization.

The headword names that unshielded quality beside 'nakedly exposed,' rather than reporting a person removing clothes. Raising his whisk, he tests whether the assembly understands, then reworks Fadeng's old account of coming out to settle his teacher's unfinished case. The description of complete exposure does not make that new test unnecessary; Ruibai still asks the listeners to distinguish his treatment from the old teacher's. A monk tells Lingji Xingguan that he has traveled countless mountains but still finds awakening through Zhaozhou's cypress difficult. Lingji answers that it is bare directly before his face. The headword counters the apparent distance and difficulty of the monk's search with immediate exposure; it does not supply a literal naked body as the cypress case's answer. Nearby exchanges in the same record rebuke a monk for merely repeating the teacher's phrase and test whether listeners know where their bows land. Those limits matter: saying 'bare before you' is not evidence that the questioner has already understood. On the Buddha's awakening day, Zhongfeng Mingben describes the true matter as impossible to name or depict, yet brilliant, round, pure and bare. He then announces Shakyamuni within the listeners' own eyes, seeing the morning star and awakening at their heads. If they do not understand, they must return to their seats and take up their unresolved question energetically. His ensuing prohibitions include neither fighting distraction mechanically nor rejecting imagined thoughts to seek truth, neither seeking holiness nor waiting for awakening. The headword's exposure is part of this current address, not actual undressing or a new historical awakening by the Buddha in that room. After Tang's gift of a communal bath, Yongjue Yuanxian asks how the monks will repay him. Learned explanations of Bhadrapala's bathing realization are only talk about food, not food that satisfies hunger; even genuine attainment still meets the teacher's further challenge. How can one give a full rather than borrowed or half sentence? His closing verse says to take off the foul undershirt and meet the present person bare, yet warns that without the lion's turning method the mountains and waters remain deep. Literal bathing supports the image, while the qualifier prevents equating removing clothes with completing the teaching. At the first awakening-day address in the cold huts of Qingshan, Tianyin Yuanxiu describes arrivals who have lost their usual bearings and stand bare without clothes. He immediately asks what the exceptional turning point is, answers with a mud ox drinking from the Wuling stream and raises his whisk as Shakyamuni shining in the listeners' eyelashes. They must see this themselves; otherwise entering the empty gate has been in vain. The headword works as an exposed, unprotected condition within this challenge. It is not a report that arriving monks were physically deprived of robes or a sufficient certificate of their realization.

Senses.Explanation: A repeated descriptive expression for being bare, exposed, and without covering. The term is attested. Its recurring parallel is 'cleanly naked' (淨裸裸); records expand it with 'without covering' (無蓋覆), 'nothing that can be grasped' (沒可把), and 'fully exposed' (全露). These textual predicates establish what the expression describes without turning it into a condition to seek. The records also qualify it. Yuanwu says that being cleanly naked, cut off from thought, bare, and with nothing to grasp has 'still not left this-side affairs' (猶未離這邊事在). Later collections likewise say that even when one is cleanly naked, bare, and has nothing to grasp, 'there is still something fine remaining' (尚有廉纖), and contrast the relative ease of being bare with the difficulty of being distinctly evident (明歷歷). The corpus has five occurrences of the adverbial extension 'in a bare and uncovered manner'.

Senses.Explanation: A red lump of flesh is the living human body described as bare meat. Linji Yixuan places the ‘true person of no rank’ on that lump and says it enters and leaves through the face; later masters quote or challenge the same bodily formula. The phrase grounds the case in the visible body while refusing to identify that flesh itself as the person Linji asks his hearers to see.

Senses.Explanation: The phrase marks a bodily surface or site—the top of the red flesh-lump—where Linji places the true person of no rank and Nanyuan Huiyong places a thousand-fathom wall. Its most frequent named use quotes Linji: "on the lump of red flesh there is a true person of no rank, constantly going in and out through the face-gate of each of you; those who have not verified this, look, look" (赤肉團上有一無位真人，常在汝諸人面門出入，未證據者看看). The phrase also heads Nanyuan Huiyong's recorded saying, "on the lump of red flesh, a wall stands a thousand fathoms" (赤肉團上，壁立千仞), followed by the unnamed questioning monk repeating the sentence and overturning the Chan seat. Later records quote both formulations, combine the phrase with the "true person of no rank" (無位真人), and use it as the location of other stated predicates. The broader form "lump of red flesh" (赤肉團) occurs 441 times, while "beside the lump of red flesh" (赤肉團邊) occurs 36 times. No exact occurrence using "inside" in place of "on" was found. The entry preserves the literal bodily wording and the two principal recorded sayings without replacing them with an imported abstraction.

Senses.Note: Nanyuan Huiyong says that on the red flesh of a living body there rises a sheer wall ten thousand fathoms high. In the original encounter a monk repeats the saying and overturns Nanyuan's seat, testing whether a lofty declaration can survive a direct move. Later masters revisit that exchange or speak the line in new hall addresses about embodied presence and an ungraspable point of entry.

Entries.SourceTerm: 赤肉團上有一無位真人

Senses.PreferredTarget: On this fleshly body is a true person without rank
SearchAliases: on this fleshly body is a true person without rank
Senses.Note: Linji says there is an unranked true person on the red flesh body, moving through the faces of the assembled monks. When one asks what that person is, Linji grabs him, demands an answer, and then rejects his hesitation. Xueyan treats the seizure as direct action; Yinyuan calls Linji’s display too public. Zhangxue warns that the case is often misread, while Yezhu asks whether the phrase belongs to abstract categories. Huanxi says it anew through seeing, hearing, and speech. The phrase points to the living encounter before a fixed identity can be named.

Senses.Explanation: Linji points to a person without rank in the flesh before him, then seizes the monk who asks what it is. The original Linji encounter and Xueyan’s and Yinyuan’s readings keep the phrase tied to a live bodily challenge. Zhangxue warns against stock interpretations, Yezhu tests it against theory and event, and Huanxi voices it through eye, ear, nose, and mouth.

Senses.Explanation: At the edge of the red flesh refers to the immediate bodily boundary. Guxue Zhenzhe says that each person stands there like a sheer wall, and Miyun Yuanwu compares the June heat at that boundary to fire. Zhang Zi's distinct awakening verse is retained, while two parallel lamp recensions of that verse are removed.

Senses.Explanation: “Stark naked” names complete exposure, with nothing concealed or added. The records reinforce it with “clean and bare” (淨灑灑) and “not a thread hung” (一絲不掛), making nakedness the observable image rather than an outside explanation.

Senses.Explanation: “There is bait on the hook” marks a saying or maneuver as something to which a respondent may rise. Yushan Shangsi applies it to Layman Pang’s line; Tianyin Yuanxiu inserts it while raising the Mazu–Shigong exchange; Poshan Haiming announces it from the seat while asking whether any fish or dragon will leap. Feiyin Tongrong uses the same appraisal after a curtain case, and a questioning monk turns it back on Linyexi.
